analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation-only addition to docs/architecture/inference.md. It adds a single table row (head line 1090) describing prompt-chunk attention: 128-query blocks, the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_ATTN_QUERY_BLOCK setting, a fused single `.causal` call for eligible full-attention chunks, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0 rollback. The supplied units (base text around lines 798-1637) contain no code, so I could not inspect the described AttentionV1.swift and PagedLayerCache.swift changes. They are not in this batch, and the doc row implies a behavior change in the attention path (TB-007). Security relevance is limited. The row describes numerical and performance execution of attention on the provider's own GPU. It does not change encryption, attestation, authorization, prefix-cache identity (T-041), the cache salt, the SSD tier, or the coordinator-to-provider wire (TB-002). The text states that vision spans and bidirectional masks, along with windows and softcap, are excluded from the fused path, and that packed paged KV keeps its own path. Nothing indicates cross-request or cross-tenant KV visibility changes. The one uncertainty is whether the underlying Swift change preserves per-row causal isolation for packed or paged batches. That cannot be verified from this documentation-only batch. A fused `.causal` mask applied to a mixed or packed cohort could in principle break request isolation, but the doc says live packed paged KV is excluded. Any code-side review should check that exclusion. No new env var or setting introduces a trust boundary beyond the existing operator-controlled DARKBLOOM_* tuning keys. No findings.
